_about: The pre-show checklist (config/ve/show-gate.json): one row per thing Krish has had to say more than once about a cut, from his Wed 18 and Tue 17 corrections. Read by `ve critic --pre` (shown to the reviewer before anything is made) and by the show gate (scripts/velib/showgate.py), which needs every row answered for the exact file it shows him. A row names `auto_rows`, the `ve qc` rows that answer it when every one ran and passed; with no row, or a row that did not run, the reviewer attests the row in one line citing a frame or a time. A row whose qc row FAILED is a failure whatever is attested. Add a rule as a row here and in config/failures.json: it then applies to every future piece. Nothing here is a new taste rule: each row carries his words.

items.text: A graphic and a photo never both carry the same point: one picture per beat.
items.krish: two concurrent visual styles trying to say the same thing over one another? why?

items.text: A graphics beat sits on a graded, focus-racked backdrop, never flat black after a photograph; figures are never dimmed or blurred.
items.krish: Motion graphics on a flat black background, straight after a full-frame photograph.

items.text: A change between a full-screen beat and a face beat is a clean cut; never a cross-dissolve over his face.
items.krish: A ghost of his face in dissolves.

items.text: The wordmark appears only on the title frame and the closing card: no icons or company logos anywhere else unless he asks.
items.krish: NO ICONS, ONLY THE WORDMARK DURING THE TITLE FRAME AND THE CLOSING FRAME

items.text: off.day is never drawn as a pill, header or label, in any cut.
items.krish: off.day is NEVER to be used ever as a tag

items.text: Captions stay off for the whole title moment: check every frame of the title hold for caption text.
items.krish: A stray caption word (find) under the held episode title

items.text: On face beats captions sit in the staged band below his face; no caption page over his face.
items.krish: Captions over his head.

items.text: The episode title is built from his spoken line, timed to his words, at full stage width, as a card that slams or slides in over his hair, never bare words over his face.
items.krish: make the title captions a card that slams or slides in I think. having naked captions over my face looks stupid.

items.text: The figure a beat exists to show fills the frame.
items.krish: The key figure (41) was too small.

items.text: The bed sits 15% under the house level and is ridden by EBU R128 loudness, never RMS; the bed level does not swing.
items.krish: The music was too loud, and the bed level swung.

items.text: A track in config/music-library.json that he approved plays with no certificate check blocking it.
items.krish: Aspire is "100% licensed"

items.text: Every restart and dead silence is cut where a quiet gap allows; any kept is named with its timestamp.
items.krish: A false start left in his take.

items.text: Something lands on his first word (a line slamming in, a clip in motion, a punch-in); the joke or twist is visible before 3 seconds; never a static card that waits.
items.krish: considering that's the first few seconds of the video, it's not much of a hook. It looks quite dull for the first 3 seconds.

items.text: His whole head is in frame on his lines; no split frame crops his head or ruins the picture above it.
items.krish: Can't cut my head off and also ruin the visual above.

items.text: On every 16:9 proof beat his take sits in the bottom-right window, opposite the left-set captions, unless a full-frame clip fills the frame.
items.krish: my head needs to be in the bottom right ... if the subtitles are going to be not centralised, then something needs to be in the bottom right.

items.text: Words over a busy picture or his take get the approved halo; a page never breaks mid-phrase and the web address stays on one caption.
items.krish: Approve halo

items.text: The piece is funny and tongue-in-cheek; plates, devices and art direction come from Codex cards; every visual makes a point land faster.
items.krish: This piece needs to be hilarious and tongue-in-cheek ... use codex for all asset production, generation, sourcing.

items.text: Every known fault is fixed before he sees the file; none is listed as a caveat.
items.krish: If you know that things need fixing, just fucking fix them

items.text: Fixes are batched and checked here; the cut is shown to him once, not once per round.
items.krish: Each round of fixes went to him as a new render instead of being checked first

items.text: When he asks for a route the engine does not have, say so in one line with the closest real route before doing anything.
items.krish: render in Codex
